questions: Does wheel_radius 0.04 m raise progress above 0.2 on the s-bend and slalom, or does max_error still reach the 0.06 m floor first?
Does steering_oscillation rise sharply with the faster wheels, which would show the controller is over-turning at higher speed?
Is completion_time measurable on any track, and at what progress does the first off-track event occur?
Are line-loss events preceded by a steady drift or by a sudden loss on the sharpest bend?

intent: Test whether ground speed, not turn rate alone, is limiting progress. Raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.04 m on the best-scoring layout (iteration 4), changing only that variable. A larger radius raises ground speed and turn rate together, so the result shows whether the off-track ends come from speed or from steering lag.
learning: Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.08 m) gained only about 0.7 points over 0.09 m, so narrowing the track has reached diminishing returns. The next lever is ground speed through wheel_radius. If progress rises but max_error still hits 0.06 m, the limit is tracking lag and the next step is a sensor-lead change at y=0.05 to 0.06 m. If progress does not change, speed is not the limit and the focus moves to mass or wheel_track.
rationale: Evidence: every run in every iteration ends off_track, with progress stuck at 0.10 to 0.19 and max_error pinned at the 0.06 m off-track floor. Line loss is now rare (oval 0, s-bend about 0.95, slalom about 0.85 in iteration 4), so sensor coverage is no longer the main limit. Iteration 2 showed that moving the sensors to y=0.07 and shortening and lightening the body both hurt, so those stay reverted. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit, because max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 m. Narrowing wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.09 to 0.08 m gave the best scores so far (57.9, then 58.5), but the gain is flattening (+0.7 in the last step). Turn rate is (vR - vL)/wheel_track, and ground speed is wheel_radius times wheel rotation rate. Both turn rate and ground speed therefore scale with wheel_radius, so enlarging the wheel should add forward speed and turn authority together. The contract needs an average of about 1.5 m/s to finish in 3 s, and progress is far below that pace. Change: wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.04 m, with everything else held at iteration 4 values (wheel_track 0.08 m, 7 sensors at y=0.05, 16 mm footprints, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg). Expected result: ground speed and turn rate both rise about 33 percent, so progress should move above 0.2 and completion_time should be measurable on at least one track. Risk: higher speed may raise steering_oscillation and push max_error past the floor sooner.
